structure: Part 14 (Declaration and confirmation), read at repos/trade-imports-animals-frontend main 4c2119da. Read in full: features/declaration (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, declaration.fit.spec.js) and features/confirmation (page.js, controller.js, template.njk, outstanding.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, confirmation.fit.spec.js), all under src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features. To state what declaration submit does, also read check-answers/refusal.js (the refusal predicate the declaration calls) and the CYA_SLUG and recoverableSave definitions in src/server/app/shared/kit.js; those files belong to other parts and only their effect on these two pages is claimed. Covered: the declaration page at /notifications/{id}/declaration (heading, five declaration statements with two bullet lists, the single 'confirmed' checkbox, the date of declaration line, Continue button, the required-checkbox error verbatim, back link to check answers, the already-submitted redirect, the review-refusal redirect, the recoverable save failure, and the commit plus submit to confirmation); the confirmation page at /notifications/{id}/confirmation (GET only, the redirect for an unsubmitted notification, the panel with title and reference number, the outstanding-documents section and when it shows, the transporting, view-or-amend and getting-help sections with every link and the create-a-new-notification POST button, no back link); Welsh copy parity for both pages (machine-draft); and every test in declaration.fit.spec.js (5 tests) and confirmation.fit.spec.js (5 tests). Unit tests (controller.test.js, template.test.js, copy.test.js) are outside the partition's scope and were not claimed.

claims.statement: The declaration page is served at the slug 'declaration' under a notification, so its path is /notifications/{notification id}/declaration.
claims.quote:
id: 'declaration',
  slug: 'declaration'

claims.statement: The declaration page collects one answer, 'declaration'.
claims.quote: export const meta = { ...page, collects: ['declaration'] }

claims.statement: A user reaches the declaration page by pressing Continue on the check answers (notification-view) page.
claims.quote:
await openReviewFromHub(page)
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Continue' }).click()
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: copy.title })).toBeVisible()

claims.statement: The declaration page has a single checkbox, field name 'declaration' with value 'confirmed', labelled 'I confirm that I have reviewed and comply with this declaration and that the information submitted in this notification is true and correct.'

name: "declaration",

claims.note: Label text: 'I confirm that I have reviewed and comply with this declaration and that the information submitted in this notification is true and correct.' The checkbox has no hint and no fieldset legend.

claims.statement: The declaration checkbox is pre-ticked when a declaration of 'confirmed' is already saved on the notification.
claims.quote: checked: values.declaration == "confirmed"

claims.statement: The declaration page shows 'Date of declaration:' followed by today's date, written as day, full month name and year (for example 7 October 2026).
claims.quote: dateOfDeclaration: 'Date of declaration:',

claims.statement: The date of declaration is always the date the page is rendered and is formatted in English (en-GB) even when the page is shown in Welsh, so a Welsh user sees an English month name.
claims.quote: new Date(value).toLocaleDateString('en-GB', {
claims.note: Inferred: the formatter hard-codes the en-GB locale while the copy switches between en and cy.

claims.statement: The declaration page's submit button reads 'Continue'.
claims.quote: continueButton: 'Continue',

claims.statement: The declaration page's back link goes to the check answers page (notification-view).
claims.quote: backLink: pagePath(journey.journeyId, kit.CYA_SLUG),

claims.statement: Submitting the declaration without ticking the checkbox is rejected with the error 'Confirm that you have reviewed and comply with this declaration', and the page is re-shown with status 400.
claims.quote: requiredOneOf('declaration', ['confirmed'], copy.errors.declarationRequired)
claims.note: Error text: 'Confirm that you have reviewed and comply with this declaration'. Any value other than 'confirmed' is also rejected.

claims.statement: The declaration error is shown both in an error summary (as a link) and as an inline error message on the checkbox, and following the summary link focuses the checkbox.
claims.quote: errorMessage: errors.declaration and { text: errors.declaration },

claims.statement: Opening or submitting the declaration page for a notification that is already submitted redirects to that notification's confirmation page.
claims.quote:
if (journey.status === state.SUBMITTED) {
    return h.redirect(pagePath(journey.journeyId, confirmationPage.slug))

claims.statement: After a valid tick, the declaration submit re-checks that the notification is ready for review; if it is refused, the user is redirected back to the check answers page and nothing is submitted.
claims.quote:
if (await isReviewRefused(request, h)) {
    return h.redirect(pagePath(journey.journeyId, kit.CYA_SLUG))
claims.note: The refusal predicate (owned by the check answers part) refuses when the notification is not ready for check your answers, has an invalid party, has an invalid stored review card, or has a document that is rejected or still being scanned. Its comment says it stops 'a bookmark or back-button' sneaking 'a stale submission past'.

claims.statement: A valid declaration submit saves the declaration answer on the notification and then submits the notification.
claims.quote:
await state.commit(request, h, values)
      result = await state.submitJourney(request, h)

claims.statement: When the submit succeeds the user is redirected to the confirmation page.
claims.quote: return h.redirect(pagePath(journey.journeyId, confirmationPage.slug))

claims.statement: When the submit call returns a not-ok result, the user is redirected back to the check answers page with no message on the declaration page.
claims.quote:
if (!result.ok) {
    return h.redirect(pagePath(journey.journeyId, kit.CYA_SLUG))

claims.statement: When saving or submitting fails with a recoverable backend error, the declaration page is re-shown with the user's tick kept, a recoverable-error state and status 500; a stale concurrency token or any other error is not handled here and propagates.
claims.note: What the recoverable-error state shows is defined in the shared layout (another part).

claims.statement: The declaration form posts with a CSRF crumb and a concurrency token as hidden fields.
claims.quote:
<input type="hidden" name="crumb" value="{{ crumb }}" />
    <input type="hidden" name="concurrencyToken" value="{{ concurrencyToken }}" />

claims.statement: A fit test proves a complete notification can be declared and submitted, lands on the confirmation page, and that revisiting the declaration URL afterwards redirects to confirmation.

claims.quote: test('submits a complete notification, redirects to confirmation and keeps the declaration'
claims.note: Despite the name, the test does not assert the saved declaration value; it asserts the post-submit redirect from the declaration URL.

claims.statement: The declaration page can be opened directly by URL on a notification that has only its origin answered; the page itself does not check that earlier sections are complete before showing.
claims.quote:
await answerOriginEntry(page)

  await page.goto(declarationUrl)
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: copy.title })).toBeVisible()
claims.note: Inferred from the GET handler (only the submitted check) and the spec's set-up, which reaches the page after answering origin only. Completeness is enforced at submit by the review-refusal check (repo-frontend-p14-023).

method: 'GET',

claims.quote: title: 'Import notification submitted',

claims.statement: The confirmation page does not repeat the date of declaration.

When the submitted notification has no documents, the confirmation page shows a section headed 'Before the consignment is imported' with 'You still need to:' and the bullet 'upload the health certificate and any other required documents'.
claims.quote:
heading: 'Before the consignment is imported',
    intro: 'You still need to:',
    documents: 'upload the health certificate and any other required documents'

claims.statement: The outstanding-items section is left out entirely when the list is empty, which today means when the notification has at least one document.
claims.quote: return documents.length === 0 ? [copy.outstanding.documents] : []

claims.statement: A notification can be submitted with no documents, because the documents obligation has a cap but no minimum and no required-one-of.

Design release 1 has a second outstanding bullet for animal identifiers, which the confirmation page does not show yet; it is held back on the open identifier-completeness decision (what counts as a complete identifier record), recorded on inc-153 in the parity backlog.

A consignment declaring a single identified species can be submitted with no identifier record saved, because the identifier obligation only asks for a record where more than one commodity line carries a typed identifier set.

claims.note: The slice is silent on a confirmation email or a 'what happens next' section for the notification itself; recorded so the reconciler can weigh it against design sources.
